correctness.rationale: The source minimal H-description is exact. Permutation averaging proves that every feasible radius is feasible at a diagonal center. For subset size k, the lower-coordinate clearance and normalized upper-facet clearance intersect at the displayed r_k. After the substitution y=sqrt(k), the derivative of r_k has a strictly decreasing numerator, so the continuous profile has a single interior maximum and its minimum is attained only at k=1 or k=n. The active shifted facets then force the unique diagonal center and give the exact tangent-facet counts in every phase.

value.rationale: Parking-function polytopes are a recent natural family motivated by a Stanley problem and connected to partial permutahedra, Pitman--Stanley polytopes, generalized permutahedra, and polymatroids. The theorem treats the full all-dimensional two-parameter family, not a numerical slice, and reveals a sharp metric phase transition: exponentially many potential upper facets reduce to two controlling orbits, with a discontinuous change in the contact pattern. The classical parking-function polytope receives an explicit Euclidean inradius and a sparse n+1-facet support certificate as a central corollary.
